findings.title: The cached experiment read-back form shares the live account's metadata objects, so a record can be served that is neither the account handed over nor the record its digest names (regression introduced in round 8)
findings.evidence: src/engcore/mind/world/owners.py:348 `payload = exp.to_dict()` (round 7's `copy.deepcopy(exp.to_dict())` was dropped); :352-356 `rebuilt = ScientificExperiment.from_dict(payload)`, `back = rebuilt.to_dict()`, `cached = (content, back, _sha_json(rebuilt), ...)`; :359 `back = copy.deepcopy(back)` serves a copy of the CACHED form. ScientificExperiment copies metadata shallowly (src/engcore/scientific/experiments/experiment.py:329 `dict(sorted(self.metadata.items()))`, :352 `metadata=dict(payload.get("metadata", {}))`), so the cached `back` holds the first account object's metadata value objects. The cache is hit whenever the new account's content digest equals the cached one (owners.py:351), even when the account was replaced by another object. Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-forge/e352a8b8-4d77-5787-bd23-1bcc1dda83b7/scratchpad/review_r9/B-architecture/p01_cache_shares_live_metadata.py at ceaf8cd prints: account handed over (E2) metadata ['calibrated']; served payload metadata ['calibrated', 'REWRITTEN-ON-THE-OLD-OBJECT']; served record digest == digest re-derived from its own payload: False; admission 2 FEASIBLE admitted; replay of admission 2: replay_dependency_unavailable. The same probe against a 15725ec src copy prints served ['calibrated'], digest consistent True, replay reproduced. README section 4 states 'A pinned snapshot serves detached copies of the records it observed ... with the digest replay derives', which this case contradicts.
findings.reproduction: cd /home/user/forge && PYTHONPATH=/home/user/forge/src:/home/user/forge /home/user/.forge-venv/bin/python /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-forge/e352a8b8-4d77-5787-bd23-1bcc1dda83b7/scratchpad/review_r9/B-architecture/p01_cache_shares_live_metadata.py (gen1 pool; E1.metadata['notes']=['calibrated']; admit; the execution side restores the experiment as E2 = from_dict(deepcopy(E1.to_dict())); the old E1's metadata list is appended in place; admit again; AdmissionRecord.of; replay_admission).
findings.why: Round 8 promised that an experiment is served in its owner's read-back form with that read-back's digest, the form replay uses (D8-F2/B8-m4). Because the cached form is not detached from the first account object, the served payload can carry another object's later state under an older digest. The admission's decided fields (accounting, budget) are fresh dicts and stay correct. So the effect is limited to the record: an admission that live verification admits and records, and that replay then refuses. This fails closed and admits nothing wrong. Concurrent in-place mutation of metadata between `content` and the deepcopy tears the record the same way.
findings.fix: Detach before reading back and caching. Either restore `payload = copy.deepcopy(exp.to_dict())`, or better (see B9-m2) canonicalize to plain JSON types first, for example `json.loads(to_json(_Payload(exp.to_dict())))` after an exact-type check, and cache only detached data. Add a control: replace the account by an equal-content independent copy, mutate the old object's metadata, then assert that the served payload equals the handed account's to_dict(), that rederive() gives the record digest, and that replay is REPRODUCED.

findings.question: Q4/Q7 (availability; a narrow return of B7-m3 introduced by the round-8 fix; not an admission or dispatch defect, not a PARTIAL reason)
findings.title: The round-8 locked read-back runs execution-side hooks inside account records while it holds the follower's lock. A hook that waits on an admitting thread hangs the desk, and a hook that reads through the reader self-deadlocks.
findings.evidence: owners.py:383-384: `with self._lock: for key, got in snapshot._read_back().items()`. Under that lock, _account (owners.py:348-359) runs `exp.to_dict()`, which sorts execution-side metadata keys (experiment.py:329: `dict(sorted(self.metadata.items(), ...))`). It also runs `_sha_json`/`to_json`, which delegates to any metadata object's `to_dict()` (serialization.py:133-134), and `copy.deepcopy(back)` (owners.py:359). The re-entrancy guard is set only while accounts() runs (owners.py:413-422: `active` is reset in `finally` before `_observe_all`). A read-through from inside the read-back therefore reaches `with self._lock` again on a non-reentrant `threading.Lock` (owners.py:441). The round-8 control `test_the_execution_side_is_never_called_under_the_followers_lock` (test_authority_review_r8.py:94-106) checks accounts() only. README §4 (README.md:152-156) and the docstring (owners.py:300-301) say only that accounts() runs without the lock. Round 7's B7-m3 fix (README §9:398-399, 'no lock held across the execution side's accounts() or the read-backs') is partly reversed. The round-8 lens-D probe review_r8/D-replay-stale/d01_unlocked_readback_rollback_race.py:25-32 is such a hook: `SlowKey.__lt__`, an execution-side metadata key, waits on the main thread's dispatch. Its output on 27b9f71 (d01_27b9f71.txt), whose pin also held the lock across the read-back, was a refusal only after the hook's wait returned.
findings.reproduction: Static reading. Adapt d01 by replacing `main_done.wait(3)` with `main_done.wait()`. At ceaf8cd, V1 holds the follower lock inside SlowKey.__lt__ (owners.py:348, under 383) and waits for the main thread. The main thread's re-dispatch calls pinned() -> _observe_all and waits for the same lock. Neither thread proceeds. Not executed by this lens.
findings.why: No wrong admission or dispatch: the outcome is a hang, which fails closed. But the stated contract ('the execution side is never called under the follower's lock'; accounts() 'may take its own locks') is wider than the code. The round-7 deadlock class returns through the account records' own serialization hooks, and an execution side cannot read that limit from the README.
findings.fix: State the contract exactly in owners.py:300-301, README §4 and the test name. accounts() runs without the lock. The read-back runs the owners' serialization of the handed records under the lock, including any hooks of execution-side metadata objects, and such hooks must not block on an admitting thread or read through the reader. Rename the r8 test to '..._accounts_is_never_called_under_the_followers_lock'. Optionally keep the thread-local flag set across `_observe_all`, so that a read-through from a hook raises OwnerUnavailable instead of hanging, and add a control with a d01-style key whose hook reads through the reader.
